stem: A parent refuses a recommended treatment for a younger child and the team is concerned that the refusal may place the child at risk of significant harm; what additional step may need to be considered?

options.text: Waiting until the child is an adult
Ignoring the refusal if one parent agrees

explanation: A mandatory report may need to be considered when parental refusal of treatment places a child at risk of significant harm. In that situation, the issue becomes a child protection concern rather than a routine consent disagreement.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a mandatory report may be required when refusal of treatment creates a risk of significant harm to a child.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because discharge does not address an ongoing child protection concern.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because delaying action until adulthood leaves the child exposed to potential harm.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because one parent’s agreement does not remove the concern if significant harm is still possible.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a sibling cannot make treatment decisions for a younger child.
